source: 1,000 top videos of the last 120 days across 20 niches + the uploads of 14 channels under 13 months old (YouTube Data API), their in-video frames, and web research (RPM, YPP 2027, policy). Full write-up: research/STRATEGY_2026-11.md
lessons: Topics that win in our genre: the hidden engineering of an everyday object (a road reflector, a guardrail end, a washer, a faucet), a survival or danger scenario explained with real physics, how a familiar machine works, and the evolution of an everyday invention. Plain food or body trivia does far less.

Titles: short and concrete, 4-8 words, pointing at ONE object or moment: 'Why This Yellow Box Eats Guardrails', 'A Power Line Just Fell on Your Car', 'Could You Survive a T. Rex by Standing Still?', 'The Genius Way to Weld Steel With Electricity', 'How Ambulances Turn Traffic Lights Green'. Patterns only - never copy a title.
The hook is a situation the viewer is put in, or an object they have seen but never understood - not a fact statement.
Every line shows exactly what it says: one clear subject filling the whole screen.
30-45 s Shorts get the most views in science, animals, space and geography; 60-90 s get about twice the likes per view. Keep 35-45 s unless the idea truly needs more.
The fastest-growing channels post 2-6 times a week and each video is a strong, different idea; volume channels posting daily have far lower medians. Never make a weak video just to fill a slot.
